operations.comment: ; Super Off Road (USA): readable source, round 12.
; Physical storage uses org; execution aliases use base. All assets stay local.
; 518730 classified bytes; 5558 unknown bytes. Static structure does not prove natural reachability.
; Cold entry: switch to native mode, set DP/DB to zero and put the stack at $01FF.
; Initialize video and audio while blanked, clear frontend state and enter the attract/frontend dispatcher.
; The final call selects the first track descriptor; race initialization follows physically.
; Execution: main CPU $008000; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Blank the display before replacing track-dependent video and world state.
; Initialize four truck palette words, headings, movement accumulators and lap counters, then load terrain, route, graphics, HUD and objects.
; Enable NMI and automatic joypad reads only after initialization. $052F lets the first prepared frame return instead of entering the race loop.
; The unexplained $C8 per-truck counters are initialized here; their game meaning remains uncertain.
; Execution: main CPU $0080AA; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Wait for the next NMI after the ready transition. If the race selector is nonzero, send command 1 with host music selector (track_order & 7)+6 in APU port 3.
; The SPC decrements that selector, selecting songs 5..12. Native mode and DB/DP zero follow the inspected caller; SEP sets byte registers locally. Fall through to the existing race continuation.
; Frame dispatcher: wait for vblank, collect input, then update movement, collisions, AI, sprites, track objects and HUD.
; $88 selects the frame's rendering mode. A nonzero $052F returns after this prepared frame; ordinary play continues through the separate race-end checks.
; Execution: main CPU $008198; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Return to the race initializer when its one-frame flag is set. This RTS shares the surrounding scheduler's caller stack.
; Execution: main CPU $0081CF; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Separate human-controlled play from attract/demo handling using the active-controller mask. The adjacent completion branch now handles the winner transition.
; Execution: main CPU $0081D0; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; While no winner is recorded, return to the race loop. Once winner_slot_plus_one is nonzero, run the result transition and re-enter race initialization.
; Execution: main CPU $0081D4; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; Keep dispatching race frames until the winner slot is nonzero. A winner transfers control to post-race handling.
; Execution: main CPU $0081DE; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Invoke the results/continuation flow, then increment the track-order slot. The following fragment wraps and resolves that slot.
; Execution: main CPU $0081E5; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Wrap the sequence index modulo 64, resolve its direction and track descriptor, then initialize the next race.
; The preliminary low-nibble store is overwritten by select_track_descriptor; do not mistake it for the final track selection.
; Execution: main CPU $0081ED; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Unknown physical $0001FB..$000200: unresolved role, format or relevant execution context. Raw preservation is not data evidence.
; Read one of 64 track-order bytes using the sequence slot. Bit 7 becomes the reversed-direction flag; the low seven bits become the track ID.
; Status is restored on return. The table supplies a fixed 16-track domain; reverse track 09 is absent from this natural order.
; Execution: main CPU $008200; DB=None, DP=None. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Unresolved reference bank: numeric operands retain encoded offsets where DB/DP is unknown.
; 64 sequence bytes. Bit 7 selects reversed direction; bits 0..6 select the track descriptor. All sixteen track IDs occur, while reverse track 09 has no natural order slot.
; Preserve the caller's 16-bit sound command while testing the low byte of the active-controller mask.
; Write it to APU ports 2/3 only during human play; the alternate tail discards it during attract mode.
; Execution: main CPU $008256; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Balance send_race_sound_if_human's saved accumulator without sending audio, then return.
; Execution: main CPU $008263; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Human play dispatches to its separate control handler; attract mode falls through to a Start-button test.
; Execution: main CPU $008265; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Combine all four automatic joypad words and test Start ($1000).
; On Start, discard the current return address, mark frontend reentry and jump into boot's frontend initialization. Otherwise return to the demo race.
; Execution: main CPU $00826E; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; For the current truck's word index in $49, scan the other three truck indices.
; A squared coarse distance below $28 triggers contact resolution and starts a six-tick per-truck contact counter.
; The distance helper uses Mode 7 multiplication for squared coordinate differences; axis differences at least $0A00 return the out-of-range sentinel $29.
; Execution: main CPU $00828B; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Finish the absolute X difference and reject distant pairs, then square the reduced X and Y differences using Mode 7 multiplication.
; Return their sum in 16-bit A. $54 holds the first square; the result is a coarse distance metric rather than a world-coordinate distance.
; Execution: main CPU $0082C7; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Return $29, safely above the contact cutoff $28, when either axis is too far apart.
; Execution: main CPU $00830E; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Reduce signed truck separation through quantize_signed_vector_to_lookup_index and read a circular byte
; bearing from vector_direction_lookup. Save it as contact_normal_heading ($0529). Subtract the same normal
; from each truck heading, quantize both relative angles into four sectors and pack the pair into response-
; case nibbles. This consumer establishes heading arithmetic; it adds no natural read evidence for stored
; Execution: main CPU $008312; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Grid and sine origins are encoded independently; the storage extent is inferred.

; Negate the two contact speeds, retaining the other truck's original low byte in the accumulator high byte. Compare absolute magnitudes with $20 to select the high-speed or gentle collision response.
; Execution: main CPU $00836A; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; Recognize packed sector pairs $00 and $22 as the shared speed-exchange response. Other combinations continue through later cases.
; Execution: main CPU $00839C; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Exchange current and other-truck movement values, then nudge the other heading by 16 angle units on alternating frame parity.
; A speed difference of at least $20 requests impact audio; both paths continue to positional separation.
; Execution: main CPU $0083A4; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.

; Deflect the working truck after contact: if speed is below $60, add $20; then turn heading by eight, subtracting on odd animation frames and adding on even frames. This wraps the byte heading before continuing into terrain-tested pair separation.

; Instruction boundaries require M8 only. State names assume DB00/DP0000 and the speed arithmetic description assumes decimal clear; these are semantic conditions, not observed arrival facts. No stack bytes are pushed here; the final jump shares the caller's return with the established separation tail.
; The odd-frame store branches to the final transfer; it must skip the even-frame addition. Natural reachability remains unresolved.
; Recognize the four odd-sector combinations and turn each heading by four angle units according to its side of the normal.
; The remaining combinations transfer to the asymmetric response; accepted cases proceed to terrain-checked separation.
; Execution: main CPU $008409; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Choose an asymmetric heading/speed response from the packed sector bits. Some cases reduce the current movement accumulator by four.
; Large movement values trigger impact audio before the shared positional correction. Two immediate loads are overwritten before use and are preserved faithfully.
; Execution: main CPU $008456; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Average the two truck positions, then place them on opposite sides using the contact-normal sine table and Mode 7 multiplication.
; Accept each proposed position only when the terrain test returns carry clear. Current-truck correction goes through working coordinates; the other truck writes its position arrays.
; The $0200 product scale controls the separation distance; this does not imply a physical world unit.
; Execution: main CPU $008492; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Return without committing the other truck's proposed coordinates when terrain blocks them.
; Execution: main CPU $008545; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Map a wrapping 8-bit relative heading into four sectors centered on the cardinal directions.
; The wraparound sector covers below $20 or at least $E0; remaining boundaries are $60 and $A0. Preserve Y and return the sector in A.
; Execution: main CPU $008546; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Clear three 16-byte wheel-state arrays. The internal route-loader entry masks the track ID to 16 slots and selects the normal/reversed pointer half.
; The reverse-course branch adds $20 before the shared pointer store.
; Execution: main CPU $00855F; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; The reverse-course route pointer skips $20 bytes before joining the common pointer store.
; Execution: main CPU $00857C; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; Copy 16-bit route words into $079F until a word with high byte $FF. Its low byte supplies the route checkpoint count.
; Initialize each truck's checkpoint index to one. The following internal start-grid entry selects heading data using track ID and direction.
; Execution: main CPU $008580; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Rotate the start-grid heading by $20 for reversed courses; the following common tail stores it for each truck.
; Execution: main CPU $0085BE; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; Fetch the selected start heading and apply it to all four truck heading words.
; The following path derives the grid displacement from that heading; reversed courses select $FC00.
; Execution: main CPU $0085C1; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Use the negative fixed-point grid displacement $FC00 for the reversed starting order.
; Execution: main CPU $0085D8; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; Derive starting X/Y positions from the first route coordinate pair and a heading-dependent offset.
; Build a two-by-two grid, copy positions to the truck arrays and sample terrain to initialize wheel and surface state.
; The internal copy entry at $862C commits the eight prepared coordinate words.
; Execution: main CPU $0085DB; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.
; Finish committing the prepared X coordinates for trucks 2, 3, 0 and 1. The adjacent setup has already staged these words in direct page.
; Execution: main CPU $00865D; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit widths preserve the decoded entry contract.
; References retain numeric offsets when the instruction-specific DB/DP context is unresolved.
; On odd track-order slots, exchange the prepared Y rows between paired trucks. Even slots return with the original grid.
; The prepared X-coordinate commit joins this common tail.
; Execution: main CPU $008671; DB=0, DP=0. Explicit emitted widths retain the supported decode.

; Treat A low/high bytes as signed X/Y components. Halve both unsigned magnitudes together until each is at
; most seven, then restore four-bit signs and pack Y high/X low. Return a byte index into the complete stored
; bearing grid. Exhaustive scalar modeling over all 65,536 inputs confirms 225 outputs with components -7..7;
; neither component produces nibble $8, even for input -128. This read-domain result does not limit the stored
; coordinate grid (-8..7) or establish nonuse elsewhere. Preserve caller status; DP+$28/$29 and $54 are
; scratch. Internal $8885 bypasses AI when all trucks are human-controlled.
